request: Create visitor tracking and have the cron query visitor count
title: Track visits and query count on schedule
purpose: Count real site visits in Supabase and make the scheduled database activity check read that count

files.purpose: Query actual visitor counts on schedule
files.previous_behavior: The scheduled job selected a constant value from the database.
files.new_behavior: Each scheduled run reads and prints the sum of recorded visits from the private daily-count table.
files.data_impact: Reads the aggregated count; does not write data.
files.access_control_impact: Uses the existing repository-scoped database URL secret; no new grant.
risks: The schedule fails if the migration is absent or the database is paused.
files.rollback: Restore the prior SELECT 1 workflow command; leave stored counts intact.

files.purpose: Record actual site visits in the daily aggregate
files.previous_behavior: The app had no PostgreSQL client dependency.
files.new_behavior: The Node route can use pg 8.23.1 with pinned TypeScript definitions.
files.data_impact: No direct data impact; enables server database access.
risks: A new runtime dependency must be installed in deployment.
files.rollback: Remove pg and @types/pg after removing the visit route; reinstall from the prior package lock.

files.purpose: Record actual site visits in the daily aggregate
files.new_behavior: Same-origin POSTs increment the Seoul-date count once per 24-hour visit cookie; repeat requests return 204 without incrementing.
files.data_impact: Atomically increments one daily aggregate row per accepted visit; reads the visit cookie.
files.access_control_impact: Public same-origin endpoint uses the server-side database credential; private table remains inaccessible to anon and authenticated database roles.
risks: Cookies can be cleared and automated requests can inflate approximate counts.
Database failures return 503 and omit that visit.
files.rollback: Remove the route and tracker; existing aggregate rows can remain or be removed with an explicit data-retention decision.

files.purpose: Record actual site visits in the daily aggregate
files.previous_behavior: The root layout rendered site content without visit tracking.
files.new_behavior: The root layout mounts the visit tracker on site pages.
files.data_impact: Causes client requests to the visit endpoint, which may increment aggregate counts.
risks: If the tracker fails to mount, visits are not counted.
files.rollback: Remove VisitTracker from the layout; existing stored counts remain compatible.

files.purpose: Record actual site visits in the daily aggregate
files.new_behavior: A browser mount sends one keepalive POST; a module guard avoids duplicate development-effect requests.
files.data_impact: Initiates a count increment through the API; stores no visitor identity.
risks: Blocked JavaScript or failed requests yield undercounts.
files.rollback: Remove the component and layout import; existing database counts can remain.

files.purpose: Record actual site visits in the daily aggregate
files.previous_behavior: The app had no server-side PostgreSQL pool.
files.new_behavior: A lazy single-connection pool reads DATABASE_URL for the visit API.
files.data_impact: Enables the API to write daily visit counts.
files.access_control_impact: Database credentials stay server-side; TLS is encrypted without certificate-chain verification for the shared pooler.
risks: Unverified TLS does not protect against an active man-in-the-middle attack.
files.rollback: Remove the pool module after removing the API; revoke or rotate credentials if exposed.

files.new_behavior: A private table stores nonnegative daily aggregate counts with date primary key and RLS enabled.
files.data_impact: Creates schema and table; one test visit row has been inserted; no backfill.
files.access_control_impact: Revokes public, anon, and authenticated access to schema/table; postgres owner retains server access.
risks: Dropping the table would permanently delete accumulated counts.
files.rollback: Stop visit writes and scheduled reads first; retain the table for data preservation, or explicitly export counts before DROP TABLE and DROP SCHEMA.

production_safety.operational_data: Read the production aggregate during verification and inserted one test visit, leaving a count of 1. No visitor identity or existing user records were read, updated, or deleted.
production_safety.schema_migration: Applied 20261011154857_create_site_visit_counts.sql to the Supabase project; no backfill.
external_side_effects: Created private schema and daily visit-count table in Supabase.
Sent two local API POSTs with one cookie; the first incremented the count and the second did not.

verification.evidence: Next.js production build compiled and included the dynamic /api/visit route.

verification.command: POST /api/visit twice with the same WebRequestSession; query count before and after
verification.evidence: Both POSTs returned 204; count changed from 0 to 1.

verification.command: Query pg_class RLS and anon/authenticated table privileges
verification.evidence: RLS enabled; neither anon nor authenticated has SELECT.
Modified workflow is not yet on the default branch; dispatch will follow push.

residual_risks: A browser cookie counts visits approximately, not unique people; JavaScript blocking or deliberate repeated requests affect totals.
The shared-pooler TLS connection is encrypted but its self-signed chain is not verified by the Node client.
Deployments require DATABASE_URL in the server environment; the repository only has an ignored local value.
The scheduled workflow may be delayed or disabled after 60 days of public repository inactivity.
